tbpn_example.episode_title: Google's AI Breakthrough in Cancer, Protein Powders Exposed (Marc Benioff, Eiso Kant, Dante Vaisbort, Alice Bentinck, Eric Seufert, Pim de Witte)

notes:
Research (recall): Simon Wardley, from about 2005 at Fotango, answering 'where do we attack?'. A map, not a diagram: it needs an anchor (the user), position relative to that anchor (the value chain, y = visibility to the user, running down from the need to the invisible plumbing) and consistency of movement (x = evolution, left to right through Genesis (I), Custom-built (II), Product +rental (III), Commodity +utility (IV)). Evolution is measured by ubiquity against certainty, not by time, adoption or preference. Climatic patterns used here: everything evolves under supply and demand competition; characteristics change as it evolves (uncharted, uncertain, differentiating at the left; industrialised, metered, undifferentiating at the right); componentisation of a lower layer enables higher-order value; past success breeds inertia. Doctrine: focus on user needs, use a common language, use appropriate methods per stage. Gameplay drawn on: commoditise your complement, buy versus build, ILC. Common misuse: placing components on x by time, by adoption or by how much you like them rather than by the characteristics of the stage; reading y as importance rather than visibility; drawing a value chain with no anchor user, which yields a diagram you cannot move things on.

Scout: three candidates returned (Eiso Kant / Poolside 2025-10-16; Pedro Franceschi / Brex 2025-12-09; hosts on OpenAI's supply chain 2025-10-21). Chose Poolside: a single uninterrupted interview, L4128-L4494, in which one speaker names the anchor user, the need, nine components from coding agents down to grid power, and gives an industrialisation verdict on most of them, including the one that matters most for this library, a layer with demand at 250MW and no vendor to call. The host-analysis episode (2025-10-21) is denser in Wardley vocabulary ('commoditize your compliments') but it is commentary about someone else's stack, so the value chain is asserted rather than owned.

Graph decisions. (a) Components named in the source are facts; where each one sits on the evolution axis is a derived judgement and is recorded as an explicit at_stage edge with a confidence and a rationale, never silently baked into the x position. The x position is a rendering of that edge: hide derived and every at_stage edge disappears, leaving the value chain and four empty stage markers. Nine at_stage edges in the TBPN example, seven in the classic. (b) The four evolution stages are structural scaffolding: slot stage, structural true, provenance schema, no quote, no confidence, excluded from the counts. (c) movement and play are derived, and play is the idea-bearing slot; pl2 and pl3 carry idea sentences. (d) One play is a fact: Kant states his own play on air ('we had to own that vertical stack entirely'), which is unusual and worth showing as a fact node in a slot whose typical provenance is derived. pl1 has only one incoming edge, the derived enables from m1, so it floats in the facts-only view; a depends_on edge from a play down to a component was drafted and removed because depends_on is defined as component-to-component and using it for a play would blur the relation. (e) Frontier intelligence (c4) is placed at Product, not Commodity, at confidence 0.7: Kant calls intelligence a commodity but says in the same breath that only a small number of companies can create it, which is a handful of substitutable suppliers, i.e. stage III. His 'commodity' is read as the destination, which is what movement m1 records. The delivery form, tokens behind an API (c3), is placed at Commodity at 0.85 because he says outright that it is his commodity business. (f) Fact edges follow SPEC 3 strictly: two fact endpoints plus a quoted connective. Seven of the twelve TBPN value-chain edges qualify; the rest (user-to-need joins, the coding-agent fulfilment, shell-to-energy) are derived, because the speaker names both ends in different breaths. Edge te2 (coding agents depend on intelligence) is a fact edge whose connective is spoken by the host, not by Kant: both endpoints are fact nodes and one speaker's turn states the connection, which is the criterion in SPEC 3, so it is marked fact and flagged here. (g) Classic example: an original scenario in the shape of Wardley's canonical 'cup of tea' teaching map, written as a shop owner's notes so that every fact node has a verbatim span to quote. Its Genesis band is empty on purpose, which is the point of the second play. (h) Layout: plane, x = evolution -60..60 with the four bands as regions labelled by stage characteristics rather than stage names (the stage names live on the schema nodes and the axis ticks carry I-IV), y = value chain 34 down to -68 with the anchor user at the top; a dashed guide at y=-56 separates the map from the row of plays read off it.

Validate after the scaffold: 0 errors, 0 warnings.

README child review, acted on. It reported that three load-bearing quotes lived only inside rationales and in no fact node, so the facts-only view hid the evidence for the map's main play. Fixed for the most important one in content(wardley-mapping): c7's source_quote extended from L4380 to L4380-L4384 so the component node itself carries 'If I needed to call someone for 250 megawatts, guys, there's no one you can call', with its text and the README entry updated to match. Not fixed, deliberately: (a) m3's sold-out-through-2027 evidence (L4346-L4348) is not adjacent to c6's CoreWeave quote (L4340), so it cannot join that node's span, and inventing a second component node for 'compute scarcity' would add a node that is not a component; m3 is the weakest movement on the map (0.55) and its rationale states the fact in prose. (b) ts1's codex/cursor/windsurf list is the host's market survey, not a component, for the same reason. (c) c3 (Tokens behind an API) carries no entities because its text names no company: Kant states the point generically ('you're in two businesses'). (d) The note that te4 runs horizontally was passed to the viz builder.
